coverage.assessment: The cut 'coincidences' clause and the 'Nature was kind' contrast weaken the hinge from personal nightmare to European chaos. The 'spoiled child' image also loses its setup now that the whole London-delight paragraph is gone. The Gold Conspiracy refusals, Quarterly, Westminster and piracy chain is intact.

'Their advice' in the Gurney paragraph and the closing 'They…their control' have no plural antecedent; both are inherited from the first draft. 'These were the men who succeeded' after naming only Hewitt is a small plural residue. Locations and travel sequence are clear.
The Eliot exchange is correctly attributed and paired with Adams's protest, but it ends before Adams's unspoken retort, which is the scene's punchline.

The revision drops 'He thought it a mistake; but his opinion did not prove that it was one', removing Adams's hedge on his own judgment. Palgrave's prediction remains unbelieved. The glosses invent no details.
'He was twenty years in finding it out' stays unexplained. No later theory is imported, and the retrospective 'smile at his dotage' irony survives.
Paris satire is thinned (the supernumerary line and the twenty-year ban on the Marseillaise are gone), and the London euphoria is removed entirely. The aphoristic core survives.

The 'Society being immortal…Adams being mortal' contrast and 'Society became fantastic' are cut, weakening the individual-versus-society axis of the death passage. The Washington-loved/Cambridge-unloved contrast and the rhetorical questions survive.

Pteraspis and begonia are intact at both ends. The Gold Conspiracy gloss is present locally, though its partner chapter is omitted. The chaos vision is intact but has lost its explicit 'felt as part of violent emotion' framing.

strengths: The Bagni di Lucca sequence keeps V2–V4 intact with the full Tuscan-summer paragraph, preserving Nature's sensual cruelty and the exact Substance/Person theology.
The Palgrave irony is staged cleanly: 'Adams thought not. The chances were always against catastrophes' sits beside 'within three months, his world was to be upset'.
The Eliot exchange is set as separate paragraphs, sharpening turn-taking while keeping Adams's protest before V8.
Brief, non-inventive glosses for the Gold Conspiracy and the 1869–70 Session carry the omitted chapters' context.
The rhetorical questions of the Harvard argument survive verbatim, along with the 'never played cards…loathed whiskey' punchline.
summary: The revision keeps the plan's spine. All eight verbatim lines survive, along with the Gold Conspiracy and Session glosses, the sister's death, the Nature and atheism passage, Ouchy's unexplained 'twenty years', the Paris satire, Pteraspis, the begonia and the paired Eliot exchange. There is no must-fix break. Its new cuts, however, remove several connective and framing sentences: the 'coincidences' bridge from private horror to the war, the 'felt, not reasoned' framing of the chaos vision, the Society/mortal contrast, and Adams's self-qualifying 'mistake' sentence. The revision looks shorter than the 2,700-word target, so these cuts are hard to justify. Inherited first-draft problems remain: the Eliot scene lacks its dry closing line, and two pronoun antecedents dangle ('their advice' and the closing 'They').
